mechanism_narrative: The sudden collapse of RETAIL_REC from -3.0 to -39.1 in the latest week reflects an abrupt shift to avoidance of retail and recreation venues that will persist as a new baseline behavior, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RETAIL_REC fell from -3.0 at t-1w to -39.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds its mean over the last 28 days, indicating rapid rebound rather than persistence of the shock.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week fall in TRANSIT exceeding 20 points indicates a sharp reduction in commuting and discretionary travel capacity, which mechanically suppresses retail and recreation visits that depend on transit access, over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: TRANSIT fell from -0.4 at t-1w to -35.6 at t-0w, a 35.2-point drop
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC recovers toward its prior 4-week mean even though TRANSIT remains more than 20 points below its pre-shock level.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT in the same week signal a coordinated policy-driven restriction (e.g., remote-work mandates, event cancellations) whose combined effect compounds the suppression of RETAIL_REC beyond what either series would predict alone, over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall more than 20 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES fell to -26.4 and TRANSIT fell to -35.6 in the same week (t-0w)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's decline over the next 4 weeks is no larger than what the independent WORKPLACES-only and TRANSIT-only trends would predict, indicating no compounding interaction effect.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in RESIDENTIAL (from -0.4 to +10.4) signals entry into a stay-at-home behavioral regime in which discretionary trips are substituted by remaining at home; as long as RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: RESIDENTIAL rose from -0.4 at t-1w to +10.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises toward or above its prior 4-week mean while RESIDENTIAL remains at or above +10, falsifying the substitution mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility fell from a strongly positive +26.9 three weeks ago to -16.3 at the decision point, reversing the typical early-spring seasonal rise in outdoor activity; this reversal reflects behavioral avoidance overriding seasonal pull, and RETAIL_REC will track this same avoidance pattern downward over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: PARKS mean fell from 26.9 at t-3w to -16.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds with seasonal warming (turns positive again) while RETAIL_REC continues to decline or stays flat, indicating the two series have decoupled.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week increase in GROCERY_PHARM exceeding 5 points indicates a stockpiling/panic-buying surge; once essential needs are front-loaded, consumers further curtail non-essential retail and recreation visits within the following week as a substitution effect.
evidence_refs: fact: GROCERY_PHARM rose from 3.4 at t-1w to 10.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further in the week immediately following the GROCERY_PHARM spike, indicating no substitution relationship.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in WORKPLACES mobility reflects employer-driven telework policies that mechanically reduce weekday foot traffic to retail and recreation venues located near business districts, and this depressive effect will persist steadily over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact: WORKPLACES fell from 3.1 at t-3w to -26.4 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though WORKPLACES remains at or below its current depressed level.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall more than 20 points in a week while RESIDENTIAL simultaneously rises more than 5 points, this joint signature indicates a full confinement pattern; the interaction of all three series amplifies the drop in RETAIL_REC beyond what any single series would predict, over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall more than 20 points while RESIDENTIAL rises more than 5 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact: at t-0w TRANSIT=-35.6, WORKPLACES=-26.4, RESIDENTIAL=+10.4 all shifted sharply together
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's decline magnitude over the next two weeks is no greater than the sum of effects predicted from each series individually, indicating no amplifying interaction.
